findings.text: The format string changed from `{ui_filename}` to `{filename!r}`, so the filename is now shown in repr quotes. A file named `foo.txt` now gives "Could not open file 'foo.txt': ...", which changes the user-visible message and breaks tests that match the old text. Non-ASCII or backslash paths are also escaped.

The missing-parameter message used to join `msg` and `msg_extra` with two spaces (`.  `). It now uses one space, so the message text changes and any exact-match test fails. Likewise, `NoSuchOption` now joins with one space instead of two.

The usage hint was previously an f-string with no gettext call. It is now translated, but the `{command}` placeholder takes `command_path`. A translation catalog that lacks the placeholder, or whose entry contains a stray brace, raises KeyError or ValueError while an error is being shown.

0.reason: Quoting the filename with `!r` is a deliberate change to the message format, made alongside the move to gettext. Python 3 repr does not escape printable non-ASCII characters, so the only side effect is cosmetic quoting.

1.reason: Going from two spaces to one between sentences is an intentional style normalization; the message still reads correctly, so it is not a functional defect.

2.reason: Any gettext `.format` call can fail if a translation catalog is malformed, and that hypothetical applies to every translated string in this patch; the code itself passes the correct `command` and `option` keys.
